Title: TC01 – Admin loads the Orders page
Description: Verify the admin can navigate to the Orders page and the table loads correctly with all required columns and pagination.
Steps:
1. Log in as admin and navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: The page loads and a heading "Orders" is visible.
2. Observe the filter bar. | Expected: Five dropdowns are displayed with default labels: "All projects", "All statuses", "All clients", "All panel types", "All users".
3. Observe the search bar. | Expected: A search input with placeholder "Search orders..." is visible.
4. Observe the table header row. | Expected: Columns Order #, Date, User, Project, Client, Panels, Spare Parts, Estimated, Quote, Status, Last Update and a "Row actions" column are all present.
5. Observe the first page of results. | Expected: Up to 10 order rows are displayed in the table body.
6. Observe the pagination footer. | Expected: Footer shows "Showing 1-10 of N items" and pagination controls (Previous, page numbers, Next) are visible.
Outcome:
- The Orders page loads successfully.
- All required columns are present in the table.
- The footer shows "Showing 1-10 of N items" and pagination controls are rendered.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Admin Orders page load
  Scenario: Admin views the paginated Orders table on page load
    Given the admin is authenticated
    When the admin navigates to /admin/orders
    Then a table is displayed with all required columns
    And the footer shows "Showing 1-10 of N items"
Preconditions: Admin user with Super Admin role must be logged in

Title: TC02 – Admin filters orders by status
Description: Verify that selecting a status from the ""All statuses"" dropdown filters the table to only show orders with that status.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: The page loads showing all orders; footer displays the total count.
2. Click the "All statuses" dropdown. | Expected: A dropdown opens listing: Draft, Submitted, In progress, Completed, Rejected, Canceled.
3. Select "Submitted". | Expected: The dropdown label changes to "Submitted", a clear (×) icon appears next to the dropdown, and a "Clear filters" button appears in the filter bar.
4. Observe the table body. | Expected: All visible rows show "Submitted" in the Status column; no rows with other statuses are shown.
5. Observe the pagination footer. | Expected: Footer updates to reflect the filtered count (e.g., "Showing 1-N of M items" where M ≤ total).
Outcome:
- The table shows only orders with status "Submitted".
- The footer result count reflects the filtered set.
- The "Clear filters" button is visible.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Filter by status
  Scenario: Admin filters orders by status
    Given the admin is on the Orders page
    When the admin selects "Submitted" from the "All statuses" dropdown
    Then only orders with status "Submitted" are shown in the table
    And the footer count updates accordingly
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page with existing orders of at least one status type

Title: TC07 – Admin searches for an order
Description: Verify that typing in the search bar filters the table in real time by Order #
bdd_scenario:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: The page loads with all orders and the search input shows placeholder "Search orders...".
2. Click the search input and type a known Order # (e.g., "#337"). | Expected: As the user types, the table filters in real time; the row for order #337 is displayed and non-matching rows disappear.
3. Clear the search input and type a known user name (e.g., "Daniel"). | Expected: The table updates to show only orders where the User column contains "Daniel".
4. Clear the search input and type a known project name (e.g., "Substation Alpha"). | Expected: The table updates to show only orders where the Project column contains "Substation Alpha".
5. Observe the pagination footer during each search. | Expected: The footer updates to reflect the count of matching orders.
Tags:
- The table filters in real time for Order #, user name, and project name.
- Non-matching rows are hidden.
- The footer count updates with each search term.
Preconditions:
Feature: Search orders
  Scenario: Admin searches for an order by Order #, user, or project
    Given the admin is on the Orders page
    When the admin types a search term in the "Search orders..." input
    Then the table filters in real time to show only matching rows
    And the footer count updates accordingly
column12: Admin user must be on the Orders page; at least one order matching the search terms must exist

Title: TC08 – Multiple filters applied simultaneously
Description: Verify that combining multiple filters and/or a search term applies AND logic — the table shows only orders matching all active constraints.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: The page loads with all orders.
2. Select "Draft" from the "All statuses" dropdown. | Expected: The table updates to show only Draft orders; footer shows the Draft order count; "Clear filters" button appears.
3. Select "Daedalus Industries" from the "All clients" dropdown. | Expected: The table further narrows to show only Draft orders from Daedalus Industries; footer count decreases or stays the same.
4. Type "Daniel" in the search bar. | Expected: The table further narrows to show only Draft orders from Daedalus Industries where the user or project name contains "Daniel"; footer count updates.
5. Observe each row in the table. | Expected: Every visible row satisfies all three active constraints simultaneously (status = Draft AND client = Daedalus Industries AND search matches "Daniel").
Outcome:
- The table displays only orders matching all active filters and the search term combined with AND logic.
- The footer count reflects the combined filter result.
- The "Clear filters" button is visible.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Combined filters
  Scenario: Admin applies multiple filters simultaneously
    Given the admin is on the Orders page
    When the admin selects a status, a client, and types a search term
    Then the table shows only orders matching all active constraints
    And the footer count reflects the combined result
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page; orders matching each individual filter must exist

Title: TC09 – Admin clears all filters
Description: Verify that the ""Clear filters"" button resets all dropdowns and the search bar to their default state and reloads all orders.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders and note the unfiltered total (e.g., "Showing 1-10 of 337 items"). | Expected: The page loads with all orders and no "Clear filters" button is visible.
2. Select "Draft" from the "All statuses" dropdown. | Expected: The dropdown label changes to "Draft", a clear (×) icon appears on the dropdown, and the "Clear filters" button appears in the filter bar.
3. Type "Daniel" in the search bar. | Expected: The table narrows further; all active filter indicators remain visible.
4. Click the "Clear filters" button. | Expected: All filter dropdowns reset to their default labels ("All statuses", "All projects", "All clients", "All panel types", "All users"), the search bar clears, and the table reloads showing all orders.
5. Observe the footer and the "Clear filters" button. | Expected: Footer returns to the original total (e.g., "Showing 1-10 of 337 items") and the "Clear filters" button is no longer visible.
Outcome:
- All filters and the search bar are reset to default.
- The table displays all orders as on initial load.
- The "Clear filters" button disappears after reset.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Clear filters
  Scenario: Admin clears all active filters
    Given the admin has at least one active filter or search term
    When the admin clicks the "Clear filters" button
    Then all dropdowns reset to their default values, the search bar clears
    And the table reloads showing all orders and the "Clear filters" button is hidden
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page; at least one filter or search term must be active

Title: TC10 – Admin sorts orders by Order #
Description: Verify that clicking the Order # column header toggles the sort between ascending and descending order.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders and note the initial order of the rows. | Expected: The page loads; rows are displayed in default order (most recent first by default).
2. Click the "Order #" column header button. | Expected: The table re-sorts so Order # values are in ascending order (lowest # at the top); the sort icon on the header indicates ascending sort.
3. Observe at least the first 3 rows. | Expected: Order numbers in the first 3 rows increase from top to bottom (e.g., #1, #2, #3).
4. Click the "Order #" column header button again. | Expected: The table re-sorts in descending order (highest # at the top); the sort icon toggles to indicate descending sort.
5. Observe at least the first 3 rows after the second click. | Expected: Order numbers in the first 3 rows decrease from top to bottom (e.g., #337, #336, #335).
Outcome:
- Clicking Order # once sorts the table ascending by Order #.
- Clicking Order # again sorts descending.
- The sort icon updates to reflect the active sort direction.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Sort by Order #
  Scenario: Admin sorts the orders table by Order #
    Given the admin is on the Orders page
    When the admin clicks the "Order #" column header
    Then the table sorts by Order # in ascending order
    And clicking again sorts by Order # in descending order
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page; more than one order must exist

Title: TC11 – Admin paginates through results
Description: Verify that the pagination controls navigate between pages and the footer updates to reflect the current range.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: Page 1 is active; footer shows "Showing 1-10 of N items"; Previous button is disabled; Next button is enabled.
2. Click the "Next" button. | Expected: The table loads the next 10 orders; footer updates to "Showing 11-20 of N items"; Previous button becomes enabled.
3. Click page number "3" in the pagination controls. | Expected: The table jumps to page 3; footer updates to "Showing 21-30 of N items".
4. Click the "Previous" button. | Expected: The table goes back to page 2; footer updates to "Showing 11-20 of N items".
5. Click page number "1". | Expected: The table returns to page 1; footer shows "Showing 1-10 of N items"; Previous button is disabled again.
Outcome:
- Each page navigation updates the table to show the correct 10 orders.
- The footer always reflects the current range (e.g., "Showing X-Y of N items").
- Previous is disabled on page 1; Next is disabled on the last page.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Pagination
  Scenario: Admin navigates through paginated order results
    Given the Orders table has more than 10 results
    When the admin clicks Next, a page number, or Previous
    Then the table displays the corresponding page of results
    And the footer updates to show the current range
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page; at least 11 orders must exist

Title: TC12 – No results match the current filters
Description: Verify that when applied filters or a search term yield no matching orders an empty state is displayed.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /admin/orders. | Expected: The page loads with all orders visible.
2. Type a string that matches no order, user, or project (e.g., "ZZZNOTFOUND999") in the search bar. | Expected: The table body shows an empty state (no rows) and the "Clear filters" button appears.
3. Observe the footer. | Expected: Footer shows a "No results" message or "Showing 0 items" (indicating zero matching orders).
4. Observe the table body. | Expected: No order rows are rendered; an empty state message is visible.
5. Click "Clear filters" (or clear the search bar manually). | Expected: The table restores all orders and the footer returns to the original total count.
Outcome:
- The table body is empty when no orders match the active filters.
- The footer reflects zero results.
- Clearing the filter restores the full order list.
bdd_scenario:
Feature: Empty state
  Scenario: No orders match the applied filters or search term
    Given the admin applies a filter or search term with no matching orders
    When the table is re-rendered
    Then the table body shows an empty state
    And the footer shows no results
Preconditions: Admin user must be on the Orders page
